title: Model-owned bindings in DynamicPPL
summary: PR #1529 puts conditioning and fixing on Model. Follow the stored values, the three evaluation paths, and the downstream hooks that need a migration.

blocks.text: Conditioning supplies observed values. Fixing supplies values without adding their density. This PR moves both into a binding table owned by Model, replacing CondFixContext. Model equality and hashing include the bindings.

A model argument on the left of ~ is an observation by default. Whole missing or nothing arguments, and missing elements of a top-level Array, are latent. The model draws latent values into a copy of supported storage. The caller's arguments stay unchanged.

blocks.title: Running example: two readings of a latent mean
blocks.code:
using DynamicPPL, Distributions, Random

@model function readings(y)
    mu ~ Normal()
    for i in eachindex(y)
        y[i] ~ Normal(mu, 1)
    end
    return y
end
m = readings([1.0, 2.0])
changed = condition(m; y=[1.0, 3.0])
partial = decondition(m, @varname(y[2]))
changed(Xoshiro(1))
partial(Xoshiro(1))

blocks.title: Bindings belong to the model
blocks.text: A binding records how a model variable gets its value. Select a type for its fields and role.

nodes.label: Model
nodes.text: Wraps the model function and its arguments. Its values field owns the binding table. It also stores context and removal tuples.

nodes.label: BindingTable
nodes.text: Stores roots in a VarNamedTuple, a named collection that can address fields and indices.

nodes.label: BindingRoot
nodes.text: Groups a root value, its storage and its constraints. A whole bound value may use BoundValue. Partial values can use a tree instead.

nodes.label: BoundValue
nodes.text: Wraps a supplied value. The R type parameter records its binding role.

nodes.label: BindingRole
nodes.text: Abstract parent of the three role types below. The role is a type parameter of BoundValue, not a field in BindingRole.

nodes.label: ConditionRole
nodes.text: Marks an explicit observation from condition. It contributes likelihood.

nodes.label: ArgumentRole
nodes.text: Marks an argument-backed binding. Role lookup maps its bound values to the observed path.

nodes.label: FixRole
nodes.text: Marks a fixed value. The generated tilde branch reads it without adding density.

edges.label: maps names to
edges.text: The constructor builds a BindingRoot per relevant argument name.

edges.label: may store
edges.text: For whole bindings, root.value can hold a BoundValue. This edge does not cover every partial representation.

edges.label: constrains role by
edges.text: The R parameter is constrained to BindingRole.

blocks.title: Storage and scope
blocks.text: BindingRoot also carries constraints, including the owner, role and storage for partial bindings. A partial binding such as y[2] => value needs storage at binding time. The head supports the container families listed in the PR body and rejects unsupported partial edits. The diagram shows selected relationships, not every type or field.

blocks.title: One tilde statement, three paths
blocks.text: This is selected source control flow emitted by generate_tilde. The arrows do not claim that every branch runs for every input.

nodes.label: y[i] ~ Normal(mu, 1)
nodes.text: The running example observes y unless its binding role says otherwise. Submodels have a separate path and are outside this diagram.

nodes.label: _argument_role
nodes.text: Reads the model binding and local argument value to choose a role. Local variables use _local_role instead.

nodes.label: _bound_data_at
nodes.text: Reads fixed data, checks placeholders and assigns the LHS. The fixed branch does not add prior or likelihood density.

nodes.label: tilde_assume!!
nodes.text: Handles a latent variable. Applies the model prefix and then delegates to the context-based overload.
nodes.signature: tilde_assume!!(model::Model, context::AbstractContext, right::Distribution, vn::VarName, template::Any, vi::AbstractVarInfo)

nodes.label: tilde_observe!!
nodes.text: Handles an observation. Applies prefix metadata, checks the value and accumulates likelihood.
nodes.signature: tilde_observe!!(prefix, prefix_template, right::Distribution, left, vn, template, vi)

edges.label: calls to choose role
edges.text: For an argument LHS, the emitted code calls _argument_role.

edges.label: FixRole: reads
edges.text: This branch reads the fixed value and bypasses the two tilde handlers shown here.

edges.label: nothing: calls
edges.text: A role of nothing selects the latent path for an ordinary distribution.

edges.label: observed: calls
edges.text: A non-fixed, non-nothing role selects observation. ArgumentRole-backed values map to ConditionRole in lookup.

blocks.title: Same input, different binding behavior
blocks.before: condition(m; y=[1.0, 3.0]) returns [1.0, 2.0]. At mu=0.0 its log likelihood is -4.337877066409345. The supplied argument still wins.
blocks.after: The same call returns [1.0, 3.0]. Its log likelihood is -6.837877066409346. The model-owned binding overrides the argument.

blocks.title: Removing one observation
blocks.before: decondition(m, @varname(y[2])) returns [1.0, 2.0] with Xoshiro(1). The argument element stays observed.
blocks.after: The same call returns [1.0, 0.46089361482929836] with Xoshiro(1). The second element is latent. Calling the original m still returns [1.0, 2.0].

blocks.text: fix(decondition(m, :y); y=[1.0, 2.0]) has log likelihood 0.0 at mu=0.0 on both revisions. Fixed y contributes no likelihood. These comparisons were rerun with examples/dynamicppl-1529.jl on the exact base and head under Julia 1.13.3.

blocks.title: Observation and := entry points
blocks.before: The compiler passes __model__.context to tilde_observe!! and store_coloneq_value!!. Turing at 67a9f80 specializes those calls on SMCContext and copies the resulting VarInfo into the particle.
blocks.after: Observation passes prefix metadata. Tracked-value storage passes Model. Those calls select new overloads. The tested SMCContext mirroring methods no longer handle these generated paths.

blocks.title: Observation and tracked-value hooks at the head
blocks.text: The head calls these overloads with prefix metadata or Model. The tested Turing hooks still dispatch on SMCContext, its particle evaluation context.

nodes.label: Generated evaluator
nodes.text: Source generated for observation and := sites. A tracked assignment such as saved := 2mu stores a derived value when extraction is enabled.

nodes.label: tilde_observe!!
nodes.text: The head overload takes prefix metadata rather than a context.
nodes.signature: tilde_observe!!(prefix, prefix_template, right::Distribution, left, vn, template, vi)

nodes.label: accumulate_observe!! (VarInfo)
nodes.text: Maps the observation over VarInfo accumulators. An accumulator stores an evaluation result such as log likelihood.

nodes.label: accumulate_observe!! (particle)
nodes.text: Turing overload for ProduceLogLikelihoodAccumulator. It computes loglikelihood and calls acclogp, which yields the increment to the particle filter.

nodes.label: store_coloneq_value!!
nodes.text: The head overload takes Model and sends the tracked value to its raw-value accumulator.

nodes.label: map_accumulator!!
nodes.text: Updates the raw-value accumulator selected by RAW_VALUE_ACCNAME. The callback invokes store_colon_eq!!.

edges.label: calls for observations
edges.text: The compiler passes prefix and prefix_template directly.

edges.label: calls
edges.text: The selected head handler calls accumulate_observe!!.

edges.label: dispatches for particle accumulator
edges.text: This source relationship applies when the VarInfo contains Turing's ProduceLogLikelihoodAccumulator. It is not a trace of every observation.

edges.label: calls
edges.text: The callback stores the tracked value in the selected raw-value accumulator.

blocks.title: The tested Turing revision needs a metadata migration
blocks.text: Existing review probes paired Turing 67a9f804e376a1fc18ed8362532458063f443864 with this base and head. For SMC and PG, the base passed 60 metadata checks. The head had 40 failed checks and 20 errors: saved loglikelihood was zero and a trailing := value was absent. These are results for that tested source revision. The author reports separate local Turing changes in the PR body.

blocks.title: Link the downstream migration used by the author
blocks.text: The PR body already reports local Turing changes. A source link to that migration would let reviewers compare its observation and tracked-value handling with the tested hooks. The related explicit-evaluation PR also describes these migration points.

blocks.title: Reused evidence and limits
blocks.text: The earlier evidence is in dynamicppl-bindings-review/checkpoint.json, particle-metadata.jl, particle-metadata-base.log and particle-metadata-head.log in the workspace worklogs. Its recorded DynamicPPL SHAs match this snapshot. Its Turing checkout is still 67a9f80 and its source hooks were inspected again. The 60-check particle run was not repeated for this document. No result here evaluates the author's unlinked local Turing migration.

blocks.title: Public example on both revisions
blocks.text: The same readings model was run on the base and head using the existing dependency environments and Julia 1.13.3. It checked argument override, partial deconditioning, original argument preservation and fixed-value likelihood. Small outputs and environment fingerprints are recorded in examples/evidence.json.

blocks.title: Helpers against real definitions
blocks.text: The diff helper reported 50 changed Julia files. Reflection checked BindingRoot fields and selected tilde_observe!! signatures and bodies. Source and downstream hook searches support the selected relationships. These checks do not establish all runtime call paths.

blocks.text: No complete call graph or performance conclusion is claimed. The earlier full DynamicPPL suite results were not rerun for this document. The author's local Turing migration was not available as a source revision in the PR body.
